name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, H.R. 1, Pub. L. 119-21)
passed: Senate 51-50 (VP tiebreak) Jul 1 2025; House 218-214 Jul 3 2025; signed Jul 4 2025

provisions.name: No tax on tips
provisions.details: Deduction up to $25,000 for qualified tips; phases out for higher earners; limited to customarily-tipped occupations.
provisions.beyond: Expires after 2028 unless Congress extends it — a built-in cost cliff and a likely 2028-cycle campaign issue.
provisions.winners: Tipped workers who owe federal income tax (payroll tax still applies).
provisions.caveat: Workers with little or no income-tax liability gain little.

provisions.name: No tax on overtime
provisions.details: Deduction for the premium (“half-time”) portion of overtime pay — up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint); phases out for high earners.
provisions.caveat: Only the premium portion, not total overtime pay.

provisions.name: Senior deduction
provisions.details: Extra $6,000 deduction per person age 65+ (in addition to the standard deduction); phases out above $75K single / $150K joint income. Social Security benefits themselves are still taxable.
provisions.beyond: Expires after 2028; seniors face a higher bill in 2029 unless extended.
provisions.caveat: Not an elimination of tax on Social Security.

provisions.name: Car-loan interest deduction
provisions.details: Deduct up to $10,000/yr of interest on a loan for a new, U.S.-assembled personal vehicle; phases out at higher incomes.
provisions.beyond: Expires after 2028; only loans originated after 2024 qualify.
provisions.winners: Buyers of new American-assembled cars with financing.
provisions.caveat: Used cars and foreign-assembled models excluded.

provisions.name: “Trump accounts” (child savings)
provisions.details: Tax-deferred accounts for children; $5,000/yr contribution limit; $1,000 federal seed deposit for U.S.-citizen babies born 2025–2028. Contributions begin in mid-2026.
provisions.window: Seed deposit: births 2025–2028; accounts are permanent
provisions.y2027: First full year of contributions; employer contributions allowed.
provisions.y2028: Last birth-year cohort eligible for the $1,000 seed.
provisions.beyond: Accounts persist; whether the seed continues past 2028 is up to Congress. Long-term effect depends on family contributions.
provisions.caveat: Benefit skews to families with money to add beyond the seed.

provisions.name: SALT deduction cap raised
provisions.details: Cap rises from $10,000 to $40,000 (2025), +1%/yr through 2029; phases back down for incomes above ~$500K.
provisions.beyond: Reverts to $10,000 in 2030 absent new law.
provisions.winners: Itemizers in high-tax states (NY, NJ, CA, etc.).
provisions.caveat: Most benefit goes to higher-income itemizers; a “SALT torpedo” can hit incomes near the phase-out.

provisions.name: Charitable giving changes
provisions.details: Starting 2026: non-itemizers can deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of cash gifts; itemizers face a 0.5%-of-AGI floor; value for top-bracket donors capped at 35%.
provisions.beyond: Permanent. Broadens giving incentives for small donors, trims the benefit for large itemizers.
provisions.winners: Small/regular donors who take the standard deduction.
provisions.caveat: Large donors may see a smaller deduction.

provisions.name: Medicaid work requirements & eligibility changes
provisions.details: 80 hrs/month work or qualifying activity for expansion adults 19–64; 6-month eligibility redeterminations; limits on provider taxes and state-directed payments phased in from 2028.
provisions.window: Requirements begin by Jan 1 2027 (states may delay to 2028 with approval)
provisions.y2027: Work requirements start; coverage losses begin to appear.
provisions.y2028: Provider-tax limits start phasing in — pressure on state budgets and rural hospitals.
provisions.beyond: CBO: ~10M fewer on Medicaid/CHIP by 2034; permanent unless repealed.
provisions.caveat: Administration/supporters dispute that these are “cuts” rather than anti-fraud reforms; CBO scores them as spending reductions.

provisions.name: SNAP changes
provisions.details: Expanded work requirements; states take on a share of benefit costs beginning FY2028 depending on error rates.
provisions.beyond: State budgets absorb new costs; benefit levels may shrink in high-error states.
provisions.caveat: Impact varies widely by state administration quality.

provisions.name: ACA marketplace & Planned Parenthood
provisions.details: Tightens marketplace verification/enrollment rules; one-year Medicaid funding bar for certain abortion providers (Planned Parenthood).
provisions.beyond: Interacts with expiration of enhanced ACA subsidies, which is a separate fight.
provisions.caveat: Separate from Medicaid cuts but part of the same ‘medical funding’ debate.

provisions.name: Debt limit increase
provisions.details: Raises the statutory debt limit by $5 trillion.
provisions.beyond: Defers the next debt-limit standoff; interest costs on higher debt compound.
provisions.caveat: Adds to the long-run debt path.
